Added evidence_chunk_retrieved tracking, retrieval_conditioned_chunk_grounding_metrics, and chunk_retrieval_coverage to backend/evaluation/evaluator.py; added bootstrap_precision_recall_ci to backend/evaluation/metrics.py. Reported strictly as a diagnostic decomposition alongside the unconditional headline, per explicit instruction -- never as a replacement for it.

incident_log.issue: User requested pursuit of 90+ score by 7pm deadline; RQ2 classifier retrain was scoped as the highest-leverage lever (see incident context).
incident_log.fix: Before committing GPU time to training, directly re-read the tech proposal and Week-4 pseudocode PDFs (via a dedicated verification pass) for the S5/RQ2 specification. Found explicit, deliberate language: S5 is specified as Mistral-7B "prompted, no fine-tuning" (pseudocode p.2), unlike S2/S6 which ARE QLoRA fine-tuned -- a design choice, not an oversight. Training a classifier to close the RQ2 gap would therefore violate the proposals own explicit architecture to inflate a metric. Declined to pursue this path even though it was requested and would likely have raised the score, and reported the finding transparently rather than proceeding quietly. The RQ2 shortfall is now correctly characterized as a genuine tension in the proposals own design (ambitious target + non-fine-tuned method mandate), not an implementation gap.

incident_log.issue: Ablations suite crashed on the finbert baseline step (RuntimeError: Insufficient CUAD labels) after 6 variants completed. Root-caused rather than worked around: settings.cuad_dataset resolves to a clause-classification schema (fields: file_name, clause, pages, class_id, label) but finbert_domain_baseline() was written for an older QA-style schema (question, answers) -- every row silently returned question=None/answers=None, so zero labels were ever collected across 1500 scanned rows.
incident_log.fix: Rewrote the field access to use the actual schema (label for category, clause for text). Also found and fixed a second, more serious bug while fixing the first: the original code treated ANY unmapped CUAD category as "Safe", directly violating configs/risk_taxonomy.yaml's own documented safe_policy ("Unmapped CUAD categories are excluded and must never be silently converted to Safe"). Replaced with a small, disclosed whitelist of administratively-safe-by-definition categories (Parties, Document Name, Effective Date, Agreement Date, Governing Law) local to this baseline function, not the main taxonomy. Verified the fix collects 5 of 6 classes (Liability Waiver 649, Hidden Fee 287, Safe 250, Auto-Renewal 231, Penalty Clause 83); confirmed via a separate 8000-row scan that Data Sharing genuinely does not exist as a category in this CUAD variant at all -- consistent with this project's own established finding that Data Sharing had to be sourced externally (converted_contract_nli) for FLB itself. Disclosed as a real data-supply limitation of this baseline, not patched over.

incident_log.issue: Ablations suite has no resume capability -- a crash on baseline N (finbert) would force redoing all N-1 already-completed variants from scratch (~10+ hours) on any restart.
incident_log.fix: Added resume=True support to run_ablations() (backend/experiments/ablation_studies.py) and a --resume CLI flag: on restart, loads the existing checkpoint file and skips any variant/baseline key already present, verified via zero redundant "Evaluated N/M" log lines during a live resumed run. This is a permanent capability, not a one-off patch.

incident_log.issue: selfcheckgpt_style baseline crashed: RuntimeError "No trained adapter configured for SelfCheckGPT baseline sampling" despite using the exact same simplifier_model/simplifier_adapter that succeeds everywhere else in the same run. Root cause: Settings.backend_for(purpose) and endpoint_for(purpose) route by checking purpose.startswith("S2")/("S5") to apply the .env S2_GENERATION_BACKEND=ollama override; this baseline's purpose string ("SelfCheckGPT baseline sampling") did not start with "S2", so it silently fell through to the bare MODEL_BACKEND default ("local") instead of Ollama, then failed because no adapter is configured for direct local loading.
incident_log.fix: Prefixed the purpose string to "S2 SelfCheckGPT baseline sampling" (backend/experiments/baselines.py) -- this call genuinely performs S2-style generation (same model/adapter as the real S2 stage), so routing it through the same backend is correct, not a workaround. Verified compiles clean, full test suite green. This is the third real bug found and fixed in the baselines module tonight (finbert schema mismatch + safe_policy violation, hardcoded-OpenAI ragas_style call, and now this purpose-string routing gap), each caught live by actually running the previously-never-completed ablation suite to the end rather than assuming untested code paths were correct.

incident_log.issue: Flagged for investigation: finbert baseline (macro-F1 0.69) beats the deployed S5 classifier (macro-F1 0.56) by a wide margin, and 3 of 6 classes showed 100% per-class accuracy -- raised a concern that its training sample (streamed fresh from settings.cuad_dataset) might overlap with FLB's own CUAD-sourced evaluation clauses (same corpus, no visible exclusion).
incident_log.fix: Verified rather than assumed. backend/app/services/dataset_streams.py::stream_partitioned() implements exactly this protection: a deterministic 80/10/10 train/validation/test hash split keyed on the first present field in key_fields (documented purpose: "prevents a one-split source such as CUAD from leaking the same contract into training and FLB evaluation"). Confirmed FLB's own CUAD sourcing (backend/evaluation/flb_builder.py, two call sites) uses key_fields=("file_name", "title", "document_id", "id") with requested_split="test" (bucket>=90); the finbert baseline (backend/experiments/baselines.py, fixed this session) uses key_fields=("file_name",) with requested_split="train" (bucket<80). Since "file_name" is the first field in both and virtually always present, both calls hash the same key to the same bucket -- the two samples are provably disjoint by construction, not merely assumed so. No leakage. The finbert-beats-deployed-S5 result is a genuine, clean finding.

incident_log.issue: Ablations crashed inside selfcheckgpt_style with RuntimeError: "Verifier calibration file not found: reports/verifier_faithbench_calibration.json". Root cause: this session's own earlier reports/ cleanup ("keep only necessary final metric files") deleted this file, mistakenly treating it as a superseded historical report -- it is actually a live runtime dependency (backend/app/services/nli_service.py::NLIService.temperature loads it on every verifier-calibrated scoring call, path pinned via .env VERIFIER_CALIBRATION_PATH). No earlier variant/baseline this session hit this code path: full/no_s6/no_s4_reranking/bm25/zero_shot/simplification_only were all loaded from a pre-cleanup checkpoint via --resume (never re-executed), and finbert/ragas_style do not call NLIService. selfcheckgpt_style was the first code path to actually need it.
incident_log.fix: Regenerated for real via the project's own documented calibrate-verifier command (python main.py calibrate-verifier --output reports/verifier_faithbench_calibration.json) rather than fabricating a plausible-looking value -- fit fresh on held-out ContractNLI validation data (2000 examples default), completed in seconds since it is local batched DeBERTa inference, not per-example API calls. New temperature: 2.3404. Confirms this file must be treated as a build artifact / runtime config, not a disposable report, going forward.
